answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded, degree-normalized random walks, limiting the influence of distant endorsements. If sybil identities form a cluster with few edges to independently trusted nodes, its low conductance creates a sparse external cut; with anchored trust and capped per-node weight, this bottleneck bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. Min-cut transitivity bounds constrain how far that influence can spread, whether the cluster is labeled reef, wharf, or canyon.
